Aquarius features three types of cards: Elements, Goals, and Actions. Element cards are played kind of like dominoes, with each player trying to win by connecting seven panels of one particular element. Goal cards determine which element each player is going after, and Action cards allow players to shake up the action in five different ways. The game is fast, fun, colorful, and easy to learn. Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Setup 2 Gameplay 3 End of Game 4 Special Cards 4.1 Action Cards 4.2 Wild Cards Setup Each player gets a different secret Goal (Air, Earth, Fire, Space, Water), along with 3 cards as their initial hand. The remaining Goals are placed as invisible players. The centre starts with a non-Action card. Gameplay On a player's turn, they must draw a card, then play a card. If the played card is an Element card, place it such that at least a portion of one edge matches an Element of a neighbor card's edge. Cards may not be placed perpendicular to one another, skewed, or misaligned. If the Element card played cause 2/3/4 different Elements to form connections at the same time, draw 1/2/3 extra card(s). If the played card is an Action card, discard it and activate its function. End of Game At any time, if a chain of seven connected panels of a (visible) player's Goal's Element is in place, that player wins. Special Cards Action Cards Trade Goals: Swap your Goal with another player's (including invisible players). Shuffle Goals: Shuffle all Goals and redeal them. Trade Hands: Swap your hand with another player's. Shuffle Hands: Shuffle all cards in players' hands and deal them back evenly, starting with yourself. Zap a Card: Select an Element card on the table and add it to your hand. Move a Card: Select an Element card on the table and move it to a new legal position. The card can be rotated. Zap a Card or Move a Card can be used to create isolated cards. Wild Cards When played as an Element card, Wild cards are all Elements at the same time. However, you cannot draw extra cards when playing a Wild card as an Element card. Wild cards can also be played as any Action card. [Rating: 2/10] It might work as a kids game but I found it too uncontrollable (switchable game goals?). Didn't enjoy this at all.

[Rating: 2/10] [Played 1 time] Luck is crucial. Your decisions will have no impact on the result.

[Rating: 2/10] Only played it the once but didn't like it. Draw cards, play cards, not much thought or strategy and not that much fun

[Rating: 2/10] Dominoes + Fluxx + art. Broken unless the "shuffle goals" cards are removed. Otherwise completely random as to who wins.

[Rating: 2/10] Components: Another tile game with cards as the tiles; I would definitely prefer tiles, though perhaps not at the cost it would necessitate. The art is simple and somewhat appealing.  Experience: A bit boring, as I try to link together tiles featuring my secret objective. Either I go straight for the objective and gives myself away, or I 'bluff', as the game suggests, but risk handing the game to my opponent.  Last Played: 2002-01-01 Eagerness to Play Again: No Desire  Plays (1): ? players: 1

[Rating: 2/10] Usually I don't like to say "this game sucks" but... This game sucks. It's like merging Fluxx with dominoes while leaving aside all the fun and only picking the worst of each. The chaos is so high that it's only playable with two: with more players it will only get more and more frustrating.  I must say that the initial idea is good, but its implementation fails completely mainly due to a group of cards: the "change goal" ones. It should be prohibited by law a game in which secret objectives can be interchanged, and this is the proof. Sadly, if you remove the cards that allow you this the game

[Rating: 2/10] Random card laying game. Goals shifting between players and many turns in between yours ensures that board state will be hugely in flux. Pointlessly random for me. Colorful art.

[Rating: 2/10] Bought for 4 € from a Facebook marketplace. H likes Looney Labs games.  Nice art but otherwise this "game" is the definition of distilled horror. It just keeps dragging on. Uninteresting.  - - -  Resides at my grandparent’s place.

[Rating: 2.5/10] At least the artwork is nice. I'm told it's a descendant of Fluxx, which makes sense since it's so random (I've never played Fluxx, but I know of it). Cards that make players trade goals, trade hands, or shuffle everyone's hands and deal the cards back out? No thanks.
